Inside Operation Nemo

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Behind-the-scenes with the SAPS Organised Crime Unit investigating predator teachers in elite private schools. Could there be a paedophile ring?

Unique Selling Point:
Interview with Colonel Heila Niemand, Head of Operation Nemo, at the Unit's state-of-the-art offices in Menlyn, which have been donated by FNB. This facility houses various SAPS units, including Cyber Crime, and supports them in their fight against crime. The bank gives access to their resources, and once a week banking staff lend their expertise.
Tall, softly spoken, unshakeable - Colonel Heila Niemand from SAPS Organised Crime Unit has investigated the cases in the Eastern Cape, taking statements from parents, victims and schools – working with the resources at her disposal to build a case of organized crime against the perpetrators.
But the prosecution of these known offenders in the Eastern and Western Cape has been frustrated because NONE of the victims are willing to testify in court.
Hopefully our broadcast will encourage victims to step forward.



Summary:
Paedophile teachers/coaches in elite private schools have been targeted by a task team made up of podcaster Deon Wigget, Women and Men Against Child Abuse, SAPS and lawyer Ian Levitt. Dubbed Operation Nemo because of the association with aquatic sports, they have connected the dots between a ring of convicted or exposed paedophiles. The names on the list are the following:

David McKenzie: former water polo coach at St Andrew's, Grahamstown, attended Grey High School, PE

Dean Carelse: former water polo coach at Grey High school, convicted of possession of child pornography in Australia

Neil Malherbe: Head of Penryn Prep in White River, convicted of possession of child pornography, later overturned because of legal technicality.

There is evidence of WhatsApps, voice notes or photos linking these three generations of predators. These were found by Deon Wiggett on David McKenzie's cell phone which was seized by the police when investigating the death of Thomas Kruger, a St Andrew's boy who committed suicide at the school in 2018. His father, Charl Kruger, believes that his son was sexually groomed by McKenzie, his housemaster and water polo coach.
Deon Wiggett named the cellphone Deep Throat as it coughed up the secrets of McKenzie and the boys he was inappropriately close to at St Andrews. All this information is now in the possession of Colonel Niemand. Although there is evidence that several boys have been victimised by both McKenzie and Carelse, none of them are willing to come forward and testify in court.

Further information:
However, in Johannesburg it's a different story. Colonel Niemand has now taken over the investigation of the St John’s paedophile. BN taught water-polo and rock climbing at St John’s college in Johannesburg between 2002 and 2014. He was also the Head of Pastoral Care in the Prep School, a position of trust which gave him unsupervised alone-time with vulnerable boys. One such boy was Julio Mordoh who signed an affidavit attesting to his sexual abuse by BN between the ages of 9 and 12. Julio committed suicide in November 2022 at the age of 20.
However, Julio is NOT alone. Since taking over as Investigating Officer on 1 July, the Colonel has gathered 14 statements from victims, now adult men, who are willing to testify against BN Even though teachers and the school matron had reported suspicious behaviour to the Principal, BN was simply made to sign a letter of warning.
After 2014 BN moved to Saheti school and then to Heron Bridge, where he was Deputy Head of the Prep school when the first charges were laid in November 2021.
Some of the abuse happened on the school camp in the Magaliesberg. BN appeared in the Rustenburg Court on 9 October 2023, and again on 7 December 2023. Worryingly, BN is still a Director of Maretlwane Experience, a company which still hosts school tours to the Magaliesberg camp.

Press Release:


Operation Nemo
In a string of WhatsApp messages between a schoolteacher and a young boy, police investigator Colonel Heila Niemand found some startling evidence. Vulnerable students were allegedly being sexually groomed by a person in a position of authority at one of the country’s most prestigious private boys’ schools. The text messages, voice notes, and photos also revealed that several boys had fallen victim to predators at more than one elite school. The seasoned Organised Crime Unit investigator was confronted by sinister cases of inappropriate behaviour and sexual abuse by teachers and sports coaches. Now the team behind Operation Nemo, a special task force investigating a network of paedophiles inside some elite private schools, is hoping to turn evidence into convictions.
Producer: Kate Barry | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


V/O: Two elite private schools at opposite ends of the country…
…among the oldest and most esteemed institutions in the land.

Both rocked by allegations of child sexual abuse.

Teresa: The last thing that would cross my mind is that he would be put into one of the most expensive schools in Johannesburg and violated as a child.

V/O: This is the story of Operation Nemo, the police investigation into the targeting of children by predator coaches in top schools.

Heila: I think I’ve got this inner fire in me that really wants to investigate crimes against women and children. This is my passion, so I feel fortunate to be able to be in this position to investigate these types of cases.

V/O: Trained by the FBI, Colonel Heila Niemand is part of an international task force that investigates crimes against children. These hi-tech offices in Pretoria are sponsored by a private financial institution. It’s a collaborative space for international and local law enforcement agencies.

Link: When you think of a police station, you don’t think of a building like this building. Colonel Niemand has access to state-of-the-art resources to assist her in bringing these perpetrators to book.

V/O: This is where the Colonel heads up Operation Nemo, which falls under the Organised Crime Unit.

Heila: Whenever there’s a link between two or more specific targets, it then actually comes down to an organised crime syndicate. And especially identifying different water polo coaches in this specific crime.

V/O: The investigation started with the former water polo coach at St Andrew’s in Grahamstown, David Mackenzie. In the weeks and months that followed it would lead them to other schools and other alleged perpetrators.
When Charl Kruger’s son Thomas arrived at St Andrew’s boarding school in 2016, this was his sport of choice.

Charl: Tom’s favourite teacher from the outset of him being at Saint Andrews was David Mackenzie, who was their Deputy Housemaster, water polo coach, his mentor and teacher and spiritual guidance counsellor. He couldn't stop talking about McKenzie; he absolutely loved him; he would do anything for him.

Masa: And what were your initial thoughts?

Charl: He was unbelievably charming, likable, just a nice guy. We kind of believed that he had Tom's back.

V/O: But when Tom showed the family a special place called Pride Rock on his 16th birthday, Charl became uneasy.

Charl: So, I said to him boy, how did you get to this place? Where did, how did you find it? And he said to me it's mine and Mr. Mackenzie's favourite place this, Dad. And that's when the warning bells started ringing and I said to myself this can’t be right. How is a teacher taking my child out of school to a place that’s 7 kilometres outside Grahamstown? What was going on here?

Mackenzie: Hello M-Net and Survivor. My name is David Mackenzie, I’m 29 years old. I’m from Port Elizabeth, South Africa.

V/O: This video of David Mackenzie auditioning for Survivor was filmed at Pride Rock - by Tom Kruger – clear evidence of their special relationship.

Masa: Did any of the other teachers or parents voice concerns about Mackenzie?

Charl: There were numerous parents that voiced concerns about Mackenzie, as far back as 2016.

V/O: These complaints went nowhere, as the headmaster at the time felt there was no evidence of wrongdoing.

V/O: But when Mackenzie signed a boy out of the sanatorium - or sick bay - to spend the night in his flatlet, the school confiscated the boy’s cell phone. His WhatsApp messages are shocking evidence of an inappropriate relationship between teacher and pupil.

TXT: I loved the last 24 hrs.
But this is impacting my job. I want to talk to you every day and see you every day.
We just have to be clever now nothing changes between us I promise! We can still do things.

Okay sir.

V/O: Confronted with this evidence Mackenzie abruptly resigned, and simply moved on to coach at another prestigious school - Grey College in Bloemfontein.

Charl: Tom fell into a deep state of depression when Mackenzie left St Andrew’s.

Masa: Did you ever ask Tom what happened between them?

Charl: I did, and I actually did ask Tom straight out as to whether or not he had been abused by Mackenzie. And he just scrunched up his face like this, and he went…

Masa: And in that moment, what did you think?

Charl: I thought there’s, my son, you know, you know your children, and I knew then that he was lying to me.

V/O: They took Tom out of school to recover, but that didn’t stop Mackenzie from contacting him.

Mackenzie: Ja shit, Tom. Make up your mind, I want to know what you’re doing with your life please, so I can sleep at night. So, give me information ASAP.

Heila: It’s like you can see this person is abnormal; unhealthy contact between a student and a teacher. It’s unacceptable.

V/O: Tom returned to St Andrew’s in November 2018 and joined a 21-day hike with other Grade 10s. But he was sent back to school early for disciplinary reasons - unbeknown to his parents.

Charl: The first time we heard that Tom had come back to the sanatorium was on Sunday the 18th of November, 10:42 am in the morning, when we received a phone call from Alan Thompson to say I’ve got bad news for you. And I thought well now what, you know? And he said unfortunately Tom’s taken his own life.

V/O: 16-year-old Tom was found hanging from the window of the Saint Andrew’s sanatorium.

V/O: Police raided Mackenzie’s home and seized his cell phone. In a discovery that would boost the investigation, they found damning images of half-naked boys in his flat. Here is Tom, with a bare-chested Mackenzie joining in the fun. They were first published in a News24 podcast series called My Only Story.

Link: In 2021 St Andrews appointed an independent Board of Enquiry to investigate the serious allegations made in the media surrounding the tragic death of Thomas Kruger. It was chaired by retired Judge Deyelan Chetty, and what they found confirmed Charl’s worst fears.

V/O: The evidence demonstrated that Mackenzie was grooming boys.

Heila: Sexual grooming – definitely. But nothing that can actually form any charge of sexual assault. I did interview a victim…where he confirmed that he was sexually assaulted by David Mackenzie. He gave a statement, but he said I’m not willing to go to court.

V/O: Ian Levitt is the attorney advising Operation Nemo and acting for Tom Kruger’s family.

Masa: Will David Mackenzie ever be prosecuted?

Ian: One hundred percent. The investigation needs to be fully conducted prior to all the charges being instituted against all the people. Remember, there are several people that we believe should be criminally charged. That includes the principal and others have been found wanting in the report.

V/O: Headmaster Alan Thompson stepped down after the Review Board found he’d breached his duty of care to the students.

V/O: Thompson strongly refutes and denies aspects of the Review Board Report, and says he resigned for various reason, particularly his own mental wellbeing.

Text: I strongly refute and deny aspects of the Review Board report.
Conclusions were reached without a right of reply to certain evidence.

I stepped down for various reasons, not least of which was my own mental wellbeing

V/O: The new Headmaster of Saint Andrew’s is Tom Hamilton.

Hamilton: I can’t put myself in the shoes of the person who came before me, but I can say for sure that St Andrew’s College in 2024 will be a place that will respond with agility and with urgency to any issues like that that might come to their attention.

V/O: In a written response to Carte Blanche David Mackenzie disputed the findings of the Review Board, saying they were made without the right of cross examination or a chance to confront his accusers. He claims his relationship with Thomas was only that of a mentor, coach and friend, and he had a long history of depression. He also claims the incriminating photos simply showed boisterous fun by water polo team members.

Text: “The findings of the Board were made without the right of cross examination or an ability to confront my accuser/s. I had no insight into the evidence that was given by other witnesses and could not challenge it. I dispute the finding of the Board.”

Text: It was that of a mentor, coach and friend.

Text: Such photographs record boisterous fun by members of the water polo team.
PAUSE
V/O: Then, in another breakthrough for the investigation, police also found links to other water polo coaches on Mackenzie’s phone.

Heila: All the names come up in different messages. So, you will hear about Dean Carelse; you will hear about Mackenzie referring to Dean Carelse.

Mackenzie: There’s trouble in Pearson (E.Cape high school) again! I don’t know what Dean Carelse’s done now, but it looks like he’s done it, he’s done it, he’s done it!

V/O: Before he was dismissed from Pearson High, Dean Carelse was a popular coach and house master at Grey High School in the Eastern Cape - where David Mackenzie was a pupil. He coached rugby, he took boys on cycling tours… and he coached water polo

David: I was the first person that accused Dean of being a paedophile, I certainly wasn’t the last person.

V/O: In 2002 David Smith was in a relationship with Carelse.

Masa: When did you realise that he may have a thing for younger boys?

David: The first time I realised it was when he asked me to have a threesome with a young boy.

Masa: How old was the boy at the time?

David: Thirteen.

Masa: He wanted to have a threesome with a 13-year-old?

David: Yeah, inside the Grey High School hostel.

V/O: Carelse also sent incriminating messages to Smith.

David: He said that he had a sexual event in his bedroom with a Std 7 boy - Grade 9 – that was in 2002 I think it was.

V/O: Smith’s complaints to the headmaster were ignored. And so, this paedophile was allowed to continue preying on children for the next two decades. Until he started coaching water polo in Queensland, Australia, where he was arrested in 2021.

V/O: He was convicted of child exploitation and grooming, sentenced to 2 years imprisonment, and deported.

Heila: The Australian law enforcement agencies informed us about the forensic downloads they did on Dean Carelse’s cell phone and electronic devices. They’ve identified 62 victims that were sexually groomed by Carelse in South Africa. So, he is under investigation.

V/O: But until one of those victims lays charges Carelse remains a free man. He declined an interview and refused to answer any questions.

Grey High School say there is no record of any complaints of sexual grooming or abuse by Carelse.

Text: There is no record of a learner or parent of the School having ever complained that Mr Carelse had “sexually groomed” or “abused” him.
V/O: But at this elite private school in Johannesburg, the alleged victims of abuse have refused to stay silent.

Link: While nobody has yet been willing to testify against Carelse or Mackenzie in the Eastern Cape, that’s not the case in the St John’s matter.

V/O: Julio Mordoh started at St John’s Pre-Prep at the age of 5. His mother Teresa was proud of his academic and sporting achievements.

Teresa: His absolute first love was gymnastics. He started at about five and got his Gauteng colours.

V/O: As he got older, he had to choose a school sport. St John’s recommended rock climbing where he excelled. But Julio was small in stature and targeted by bullies.

Teresa: The solution that was proposed was he would have the Head of Pastoral Care check in on him on a weekly basis.

V/O: The head of Pastoral Care just happened to be the wall-climbing coach…
and had also coached water-polo. In an office at the top of these stairs, he counselled vulnerable children behind closed doors.

Teresa: The turning point really was when he was twelve. He’d be crying in his bedroom at night, but he couldn’t verbalize why.

V/O: During the day, the coach gave Julio special attention. At break he would take him bouldering in what they called the cave: a secluded, sub-terranean room now used as a change room.
11:56:31
Teresa: There were several occasions when he came home and he asked me mom, do I stink? Do I stink like poo? The boys at school say that I stink like poo. You know, without the context I just thought they are just being nasty.

Ben: Many times, with me and a lot of other boys that did rock climbing, you would kind of be on the wall, a little bit up, and then he'd put his hands on your bum and kind of like push you up.

V/O: Ben is a former St John’s student who does not want to be identified. He claims the coach’s inappropriate touching was an open secret.

Ben: If I look at my friend group of twelve or so guys, every single one has a story. I think it did become normalised and that’s also partly why no one really said anything.

V/O: Except two teachers did speak up about what they witnessed, but St John’s insists these complaints were adequately dealt with at the time.

Text: Two complaints were taken by Prep staff to their Head during the former teacher’s tenure at the Prep, and these were appropriately dealt with by the Prep Head at the time.

V/O: As a teenager Julio struggled with anxiety and depression, but never revealed what had happened.

But another former St John’s student finally spoke up in November 2021, years after the two teachers had raised their concerns. The school issued a statement about the allegations, read to Julio by his psychologist.

Teresa: And at the end all he could say was oh, so there were other boys? I thought I was the only one. My heart just shattered. His innocence was murdered.

V/O: St John’s reported the matter to the police and asked other victims to come forward. One of them was Ben.

Masa: Can you explain why it takes so long for children to speak up?

Ben: No one ever told us that a teacher should never touch you. And I think the other part is the stigma that comes around it, especially at an all-boys’ school.

V/O: Survivors of child sexual abuse are 2 to 5 times more at risk of suicide.

Teresa: He just could not come to terms with… that he was broken.

V/O: He was admitted to a Johannesburg clinic in October ’22 but would never leave. On Saturday the 5th of November, the family were about to visit him.

Teresa: I got a call from the psychiatrist saying I’m sorry to say this, but Julio’s tried to hang himself. And at that stage all I could hang on to was “try”. And on the way I just couldn’t wait anymore, and I phoned him to say is he okay? Is he okay? Where is he? Is he at Olivedale or is he at…and they said I’m sorry, he’s gone.

V/O: Julio’s death, at the tender age of 20, seemed to spur even more complainants to come forward.

Heila: I’m sitting now with about 15 victims in the St John’s matter We also have incidents that took place in the Mpumalanga area, as well as incidents that took place in the Joburg area.

V/O: Last year the St John’s accused appeared in court on charges relating to incidents at school camps in North West. The case has been postponed and he’s been released on bail.

Link: St John’s declined our interview request, saying the criminal investigation in still ongoing. And as a potential witness in the matter, they don’t want to prejudice the outcome in any way.

Teresa: The only dangerous place my son ever went was school.

February 2024 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Operation Nemo In a string of WhatsApp messages between a schoolteacher and a young boy, police investigator Colonel Heila Niemand found some startling evidence. Vulnerable students were allegedly being sexually groomed by a person in a position of authority at one of the country’s most prestigious private boys’ schools. The text messages, voice notes, and photos also revealed that several boys had fallen victim to predators at more than one elite school. The seasoned Organised Crime Unit investigator was confronted by sinister cases of inappropriate behaviour and sexual abuse by teachers and sports coaches. Now the team behind Operation Nemo, a special task force investigating a network of paedophiles inside some elite private schools, is hoping to turn evidence into convictions. Producer: Kate Barry | Presenter: Masa Kekana Script: V/O: Two elite private schools at opposite ends of the country… …among the oldest and most esteemed institutions in the land. Both rocked by allegations of child sexual abuse. Teresa: The last thing that would cross my mind is that he would be put into one of the most expensive schools in Johannesburg and violated as a child. V/O: This is the story of Operation Nemo, the police investigation into the targeting of children by predator coaches in top schools. Heila: I think I’ve got this inner fire in me that really wants to investigate crimes against women and children. This is my passion, so I feel fortunate to be able to be in this position to investigate these types of cases. V/O: Trained by the FBI, Colonel Heila Niemand is part of an international task force that investigates crimes against children. These hi-tech offices in Pretoria are sponsored by a private financial institution. It’s a collaborative space for international and local law enforcement agencies. Link: When you think of a police station, you don’t think of a building like this building. Colonel Niemand has access to state-of-the-art resources to assist her in bringing these perpetrators to book. V/O: This is where the Colonel heads up Operation Nemo, which falls under the Organised Crime Unit. Heila: Whenever there’s a link between two or more specific targets, it then actually comes down to an organised crime syndicate. And especially identifying different water polo coaches in this specific crime. V/O: The investigation started with the former water polo coach at St Andrew’s in Grahamstown, David Mackenzie. In the weeks and months that followed it would lead them to other schools and other alleged perpetrators. When Charl Kruger’s son Thomas arrived at St Andrew’s boarding school in 2016, this was his sport of choice. Charl: Tom’s favourite teacher from the outset of him being at Saint Andrews was David Mackenzie, who was their Deputy Housemaster, water polo coach, his mentor and teacher and spiritual guidance counsellor. He couldn't stop talking about McKenzie; he absolutely loved him; he would do anything for him. Masa: And what were your initial thoughts? Charl: He was unbelievably charming, likable, just a nice guy. We kind of believed that he had Tom's back. V/O: But when Tom showed the family a special place called Pride Rock on his 16th birthday, Charl became uneasy. Charl: So, I said to him boy, how did you get to this place? Where did, how did you find it? And he said to me it's mine and Mr. Mackenzie's favourite place this, Dad. And that's when the warning bells started ringing and I said to myself this can’t be right. How is a teacher taking my child out of school to a place that’s 7 kilometres outside Grahamstown? What was going on here? Mackenzie: Hello M-Net and Survivor. My name is David Mackenzie, I’m 29 years old. I’m from Port Elizabeth, South Africa. V/O: This video of David Mackenzie auditioning for Survivor was filmed at Pride Rock - by Tom Kruger – clear evidence of their special relationship. Masa: Did any of the other teachers or parents voice concerns about Mackenzie? Charl: There were numerous parents that voiced concerns about Mackenzie, as far back as 2016. V/O: These complaints went nowhere, as the headmaster at the time felt there was no evidence of wrongdoing. V/O: But when Mackenzie signed a boy out of the sanatorium - or sick bay - to spend the night in his flatlet, the school confiscated the boy’s cell phone. His WhatsApp messages are shocking evidence of an inappropriate relationship between teacher and pupil. TXT: I loved the last 24 hrs. But this is impacting my job. I want to talk to you every day and see you every day. We just have to be clever now nothing changes between us I promise! We can still do things. Okay sir. V/O: Confronted with this evidence Mackenzie abruptly resigned, and simply moved on to coach at another prestigious school - Grey College in Bloemfontein. Charl: Tom fell into a deep state of depression when Mackenzie left St Andrew’s. Masa: Did you ever ask Tom what happened between them? Charl: I did, and I actually did ask Tom straight out as to whether or not he had been abused by Mackenzie. And he just scrunched up his face like this, and he went… Masa: And in that moment, what did you think? Charl: I thought there’s, my son, you know, you know your children, and I knew then that he was lying to me. V/O: They took Tom out of school to recover, but that didn’t stop Mackenzie from contacting him. Mackenzie: Ja shit, Tom. Make up your mind, I want to know what you’re doing with your life please, so I can sleep at night. So, give me information ASAP. Heila: It’s like you can see this person is abnormal; unhealthy contact between a student and a teacher. It’s unacceptable. V/O: Tom returned to St Andrew’s in November 2018 and joined a 21-day hike with other Grade 10s. But he was sent back to school early for disciplinary reasons - unbeknown to his parents. Charl: The first time we heard that Tom had come back to the sanatorium was on Sunday the 18th of November, 10:42 am in the morning, when we received a phone call from Alan Thompson to say I’ve got bad news for you. And I thought well now what, you know? And he said unfortunately Tom’s taken his own life. V/O: 16-year-old Tom was found hanging from the window of the Saint Andrew’s sanatorium. V/O: Police raided Mackenzie’s home and seized his cell phone. In a discovery that would boost the investigation, they found damning images of half-naked boys in his flat. Here is Tom, with a bare-chested Mackenzie joining in the fun. They were first published in a News24 podcast series called My Only Story. Link: In 2021 St Andrews appointed an independent Board of Enquiry to investigate the serious allegations made in the media surrounding the tragic death of Thomas Kruger. It was chaired by retired Judge Deyelan Chetty, and what they found confirmed Charl’s worst fears. V/O: The evidence demonstrated that Mackenzie was grooming boys. Heila: Sexual grooming – definitely. But nothing that can actually form any charge of sexual assault. I did interview a victim…where he confirmed that he was sexually assaulted by David Mackenzie. He gave a statement, but he said I’m not willing to go to court. V/O: Ian Levitt is the attorney advising Operation Nemo and acting for Tom Kruger’s family. Masa: Will David Mackenzie ever be prosecuted? Ian: One hundred percent. The investigation needs to be fully conducted prior to all the charges being instituted against all the people. Remember, there are several people that we believe should be criminally charged. That includes the principal and others have been found wanting in the report. V/O: Headmaster Alan Thompson stepped down after the Review Board found he’d breached his duty of care to the students. V/O: Thompson strongly refutes and denies aspects of the Review Board Report, and says he resigned for various reason, particularly his own mental wellbeing. Text: I strongly refute and deny aspects of the Review Board report. Conclusions were reached without a right of reply to certain evidence. I stepped down for various reasons, not least of which was my own mental wellbeing V/O: The new Headmaster of Saint Andrew’s is Tom Hamilton. Hamilton: I can’t put myself in the shoes of the person who came before me, but I can say for sure that St Andrew’s College in 2024 will be a place that will respond with agility and with urgency to any issues like that that might come to their attention. V/O: In a written response to Carte Blanche David Mackenzie disputed the findings of the Review Board, saying they were made without the right of cross examination or a chance to confront his accusers. He claims his relationship with Thomas was only that of a mentor, coach and friend, and he had a long history of depression. He also claims the incriminating photos simply showed boisterous fun by water polo team members. Text: “The findings of the Board were made without the right of cross examination or an ability to confront my accuser/s. I had no insight into the evidence that was given by other witnesses and could not challenge it. I dispute the finding of the Board.” Text: It was that of a mentor, coach and friend. Text: Such photographs record boisterous fun by members of the water polo team. PAUSE V/O: Then, in another breakthrough for the investigation, police also found links to other water polo coaches on Mackenzie’s phone. Heila: All the names come up in different messages. So, you will hear about Dean Carelse; you will hear about Mackenzie referring to Dean Carelse. Mackenzie: There’s trouble in Pearson (E.Cape high school) again! I don’t know what Dean Carelse’s done now, but it looks like he’s done it, he’s done it, he’s done it! V/O: Before he was dismissed from Pearson High, Dean Carelse was a popular coach and house master at Grey High School in the Eastern Cape - where David Mackenzie was a pupil. He coached rugby, he took boys on cycling tours… and he coached water polo David: I was the first person that accused Dean of being a paedophile, I certainly wasn’t the last person. V/O: In 2002 David Smith was in a relationship with Carelse. Masa: When did you realise that he may have a thing for younger boys? David: The first time I realised it was when he asked me to have a threesome with a young boy. Masa: How old was the boy at the time? David: Thirteen. Masa: He wanted to have a threesome with a 13-year-old? David: Yeah, inside the Grey High School hostel. V/O: Carelse also sent incriminating messages to Smith. David: He said that he had a sexual event in his bedroom with a Std 7 boy - Grade 9 – that was in 2002 I think it was. V/O: Smith’s complaints to the headmaster were ignored. And so, this paedophile was allowed to continue preying on children for the next two decades. Until he started coaching water polo in Queensland, Australia, where he was arrested in 2021. V/O: He was convicted of child exploitation and grooming, sentenced to 2 years imprisonment, and deported. Heila: The Australian law enforcement agencies informed us about the forensic downloads they did on Dean Carelse’s cell phone and electronic devices. They’ve identified 62 victims that were sexually groomed by Carelse in South Africa. So, he is under investigation. V/O: But until one of those victims lays charges Carelse remains a free man. He declined an interview and refused to answer any questions. Grey High School say there is no record of any complaints of sexual grooming or abuse by Carelse. Text: There is no record of a learner or parent of the School having ever complained that Mr Carelse had “sexually groomed” or “abused” him. V/O: But at this elite private school in Johannesburg, the alleged victims of abuse have refused to stay silent. Link: While nobody has yet been willing to testify against Carelse or Mackenzie in the Eastern Cape, that’s not the case in the St John’s matter. V/O: Julio Mordoh started at St John’s Pre-Prep at the age of 5. His mother Teresa was proud of his academic and sporting achievements. Teresa: His absolute first love was gymnastics. He started at about five and got his Gauteng colours. V/O: As he got older, he had to choose a school sport. St John’s recommended rock climbing where he excelled. But Julio was small in stature and targeted by bullies. Teresa: The solution that was proposed was he would have the Head of Pastoral Care check in on him on a weekly basis. V/O: The head of Pastoral Care just happened to be the wall-climbing coach… and had also coached water-polo. In an office at the top of these stairs, he counselled vulnerable children behind closed doors. Teresa: The turning point really was when he was twelve. He’d be crying in his bedroom at night, but he couldn’t verbalize why. V/O: During the day, the coach gave Julio special attention. At break he would take him bouldering in what they called the cave: a secluded, sub-terranean room now used as a change room. 11:56:31 Teresa: There were several occasions when he came home and he asked me mom, do I stink? Do I stink like poo? The boys at school say that I stink like poo. You know, without the context I just thought they are just being nasty. Ben: Many times, with me and a lot of other boys that did rock climbing, you would kind of be on the wall, a little bit up, and then he'd put his hands on your bum and kind of like push you up. V/O: Ben is a former St John’s student who does not want to be identified. He claims the coach’s inappropriate touching was an open secret. Ben: If I look at my friend group of twelve or so guys, every single one has a story. I think it did become normalised and that’s also partly why no one really said anything. V/O: Except two teachers did speak up about what they witnessed, but St John’s insists these complaints were adequately dealt with at the time. Text: Two complaints were taken by Prep staff to their Head during the former teacher’s tenure at the Prep, and these were appropriately dealt with by the Prep Head at the time. V/O: As a teenager Julio struggled with anxiety and depression, but never revealed what had happened. But another former St John’s student finally spoke up in November 2021, years after the two teachers had raised their concerns. The school issued a statement about the allegations, read to Julio by his psychologist. Teresa: And at the end all he could say was oh, so there were other boys? I thought I was the only one. My heart just shattered. His innocence was murdered. V/O: St John’s reported the matter to the police and asked other victims to come forward. One of them was Ben. Masa: Can you explain why it takes so long for children to speak up? Ben: No one ever told us that a teacher should never touch you. And I think the other part is the stigma that comes around it, especially at an all-boys’ school. V/O: Survivors of child sexual abuse are 2 to 5 times more at risk of suicide. Teresa: He just could not come to terms with… that he was broken. V/O: He was admitted to a Johannesburg clinic in October ’22 but would never leave. On Saturday the 5th of November, the family were about to visit him. Teresa: I got a call from the psychiatrist saying I’m sorry to say this, but Julio’s tried to hang himself. And at that stage all I could hang on to was “try”. And on the way I just couldn’t wait anymore, and I phoned him to say is he okay? Is he okay? Where is he? Is he at Olivedale or is he at…and they said I’m sorry, he’s gone. V/O: Julio’s death, at the tender age of 20, seemed to spur even more complainants to come forward. Heila: I’m sitting now with about 15 victims in the St John’s matter We also have incidents that took place in the Mpumalanga area, as well as incidents that took place in the Joburg area. V/O: Last year the St John’s accused appeared in court on charges relating to incidents at school camps in North West. The case has been postponed and he’s been released on bail. Link: St John’s declined our interview request, saying the criminal investigation in still ongoing. And as a potential witness in the matter, they don’t want to prejudice the outcome in any way. Teresa: The only dangerous place my son ever went was school.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Behind-the-scenes with the SAPS Organised Crime Unit investigating predator teachers in elite private schools. Could there be a paedophile ring?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Interview with Colonel Heila Niemand, Head of Operation Nemo, at the Unit's state-of-the-art offices in Menlyn, which have been donated by FNB. This facility houses various SAPS units, including Cyber Crime, and supports them in their fight against crime. The bank gives access to their resources, and once a week banking staff lend their expertise. Tall, softly spoken, unshakeable - Colonel Heila Niemand from SAPS Organised Crime Unit has investigated the cases in the Eastern Cape, taking statements from parents, victims and schools – working with the resources at her disposal to build a case of organized crime against the perpetrators. But the prosecution of these known offenders in the Eastern and Western Cape has been frustrated because NONE of the victims are willing to testify in court. Hopefully our broadcast will encourage victims to step forward.
metadata.Summary: Paedophile teachers/coaches in elite private schools have been targeted by a task team made up of podcaster Deon Wigget, Women and Men Against Child Abuse, SAPS and lawyer Ian Levitt. Dubbed Operation Nemo because of the association with aquatic sports, they have connected the dots between a ring of convicted or exposed paedophiles. The names on the list are the following: David McKenzie: former water polo coach at St Andrew's, Grahamstown, attended Grey High School, PE Dean Carelse: former water polo coach at Grey High school, convicted of possession of child pornography in Australia Neil Malherbe: Head of Penryn Prep in White River, convicted of possession of child pornography, later overturned because of legal technicality. There is evidence of WhatsApps, voice notes or photos linking these three generations of predators. These were found by Deon Wiggett on David McKenzie's cell phone which was seized by the police when investigating the death of Thomas Kruger, a St Andrew's boy who committed suicide at the school in 2018. His father, Charl Kruger, believes that his son was sexually groomed by McKenzie, his housemaster and water polo coach. Deon Wiggett named the cellphone Deep Throat as it coughed up the secrets of McKenzie and the boys he was inappropriately close to at St Andrews. All this information is now in the possession of Colonel Niemand. Although there is evidence that several boys have been victimised by both McKenzie and Carelse, none of them are willing to come forward and testify in court.
metadata.Further information: However, in Johannesburg it's a different story. Colonel Niemand has now taken over the investigation of the St John’s paedophile. BN taught water-polo and rock climbing at St John’s college in Johannesburg between 2002 and 2014. He was also the Head of Pastoral Care in the Prep School, a position of trust which gave him unsupervised alone-time with vulnerable boys. One such boy was Julio Mordoh who signed an affidavit attesting to his sexual abuse by BN between the ages of 9 and 12. Julio committed suicide in November 2022 at the age of 20. However, Julio is NOT alone. Since taking over as Investigating Officer on 1 July, the Colonel has gathered 14 statements from victims, now adult men, who are willing to testify against BN Even though teachers and the school matron had reported suspicious behaviour to the Principal, BN was simply made to sign a letter of warning. After 2014 BN moved to Saheti school and then to Heron Bridge, where he was Deputy Head of the Prep school when the first charges were laid in November 2021. Some of the abuse happened on the school camp in the Magaliesberg. BN appeared in the Rustenburg Court on 9 October 2023, and again on 7 December 2023. Worryingly, BN is still a Director of Maretlwane Experience, a company which still hosts school tours to the Magaliesberg camp.
